title: Contextual allocation-pattern profiler and phase-boundary exporter
author: Asha Menon
description: Motivation: latency and memory-pressure regressions often correlate with changes in allocation patterns across request phases (priming, decode, post-process). We lacked a lightweight, phase-aware allocation fingerprinting tool that 1) captures sampled allocation stacks with phase tagging, 2) derives compact fingerprints for long-term trend comparison, and 3) exports NDJSON artifacts that the reporting pipeline can ingest. This PR implements a Contextual Allocation-Pattern Profiler (CAPP) and a phase-boundary exporter to be integrated into nightly benchmarks and targeted perf runs. Design summary: CAPP runs as a low-overhead sampler inside the workload runner process (benchlab/alloc_profiler). It detects phase boundaries using heuristics (sequence token count, explicit runner lifecycle hooks, and an optional user-provided phase map), attaches a phase label to each sampled allocation stack, and computes per-phase fingerprints using a probabilistic sketch (64-bit rolling hash of top-N frames + allocation size bucketing). The exporter emits per-run NDJSON records with run metadata, per-phase fingerprint arrays, and a small histogram summary. Implementation highlights: - New module benchlab/alloc_profiler with sampler, phase detector, and sketch utilities implemented in Rust (FFI) with a thin Python runner wrapper for existing harnesses. - Exporter benchlab/reporting/exporters/alloc_fingerprint_exporter.py converts sketches to canonical fingerprints and writes NDJSON to the reporting bucket; metadata includes run_id, seed, config, and deterministic sketch seed to facilitate cross-run diffs. - Nightly CI: integrated into benchlab/ci/nightly.yml behind a feature flag (--enable-alloc-fingerprint). - Tests: unit tests and a small deterministic integration harness (benchlab/tests/test_alloc_profiler.py) that validates phase labeling, fingerprint stability across replays, and low-overhead under synthetic load. Performance impact: local microbenchmarks show sampling overhead ~0.9%-1.6% p50 wall time at 512Hz sampling on x86_64 with negligible variance introduced. Nightly collection (feature-flagged) runs at 128Hz by default to keep cost low. Rollout and usage: - Feature-gated in nightly and on-demand perf runs. - Reporting pipeline will ingest artifacts under reports/alloc_fingerprint/YYYYMMDD/runid.ndjson and a new visualization tab added to the perf dashboard will plot fingerprint drift and per-phase allocation heatmaps. Backcompat: nothing changes the runtime public API of the workload runner; the exporter is opt-in. Migration: instructions in docs/bench/alloc_profiler.md for enabling, interpreting results, and adding custom phase mappings. Related work: references ENG-1792 (phase-aware batching) and ENG-1833 (kvcache pressure analysis).

release_notes: - Add Contextual Allocation-Pattern Profiler (CAPP): phase-tagged allocation sampling and compact fingerprints. - New exporter: alloc_fingerprint NDJSON artifacts for reporting pipeline. - Nightly feature-flag (--enable-alloc-fingerprint) and docs with usage and interpretation guidance.
notes_for_operators: Feature gated; to enable in an environment add --enable-alloc-fingerprint to the bench runner and ensure reporting credentials are configured. Artifact path: reports/alloc_fingerprint/YYYYMMDD/runid.ndjson. Retention recommended 90 days by default for initial drift analysis.
qa_summary: Unit tests added; deterministic replay harness validates fingerprint stability. Local perf runs show sub-2% overhead at production sampling rates. Nightly runs initially exercised behind a flag; no customer-facing behavior changed.
